title: Modelling assumptions
examples: When we treat an object as a particle, what are we ignoring?
What does assuming a string is inextensible mean for our calculations?
If we assume the light travels in a straight line, what are we simplifying?

explain.say: Today we look at modelling assumptions in mechanics. A model simplifies reality to make maths work. We must state these assumptions clearly always.
First we treat objects as particles. This means we ignore the object's size and shape. We only consider its centre point for motion.
Second we assume the string is inextensible. This means the string length does not change at all. It cannot stretch under tension.
Third we assume the surface is smooth. This means we ignore friction between the object and the surface. Friction force is set to zero.
Fourth we assume light travels in a straight line. This is a basic assumption for simple ray tracing. It means no bending from the air.

faq.q: Why do we assume an object is a particle?
faq.a: We assume it is a particle to simplify the problem greatly. This allows us to use simple equations for motion. You might also ask why we ignore size or what the centre point means.
asks: Why treat it as a point mass?

faq.q: What does inextensible mean for a rope?
faq.a: It means the rope maintains its original length no matter how much force is pulling it. We cannot calculate any stretching force. You could also ask if the string can stretch or what constant length implies.

faq.q: If the surface is smooth, what force disappears?
faq.a: We assume the surface is smooth so we can ignore friction. This means the force of friction acting on the object is zero. You might also ask what friction force is or why we set friction to zero.

faq.q: Does assuming light travels in a straight line always work?
faq.a: It works well for basic optics problems in air. However, it fails when light passes through denser materials like water. You could also ask if light bends or what happens in different media.
asks: Is straight line path always true?

faq.q: When should I worry about these assumptions?
faq.a: You must state them when setting up your mathematical model. Stating them shows you understand the limitations of your maths. You should always check if the assumption is valid for the real situation.

facts: Treating an object as a particle ignores its dimensions and shape.
An inextensible string maintains a constant length under tension.
A smooth surface implies that the force of friction is zero.
The assumption of straight-line light path is valid in a vacuum or air.

quiz.say: A ball rolls on a surface, and you assume the surface is smooth. Which force do you ignore?
quiz.why: Assuming a smooth surface means you set the friction force to zero.

wrong.0: Tension only acts when there is a connecting string.
wrong.2: Weight is always acting downwards due to gravity.
wrong.3: The normal force must counteract the weight on a flat surface.

quiz.say: If you model a swinging pendulum as a particle, what are you ignoring?
quiz.why: The particle assumption means we only track the motion at one point.

wrong.0: The period is the result of the motion, not ignored.
wrong.2: Gravity is a necessary force for the pendulum to swing.
wrong.3: Tension is the force pulling the string taut.

quiz.say: A light ray travels from air into glass. If you assume it travels in a straight line, what are you neglecting?
quiz.why: Refraction is the bending of light as it changes speed in a medium.

wrong.0: The angle of incidence is the starting condition, not what is neglected.
wrong.2: Reflection is bouncing off a surface, not entering a new medium.
wrong.3: A change in speed causes the light to bend, which is refraction.
